hero.title: Computers, wiped clean and sent far.
hero.subtitle: We collect used laptops, refurbish them with a secure wipe and a fresh operating system, and put them into the hands of students who need them — from Wisconsin to Libya to Vietnam. What started as nine machines in 2022 has scaled to 56 this season and 156 all-time.

impact.label: Global reach
impact.text: Every laptop we refurbish reaches students who otherwise would not have reliable computing access. This season alone, 56 machines reached 1,000+ students across FTC teams and community programs on four continents — turning hardware that would sit unused in a closet into an active educational tool.

whyItMatters.heading: Why It Matters
whyItMatters.body: Access to a working laptop is not a given for a student team in Tripoli, Kingston, or Ho Chi Minh City. When Libya Team 18422 runs Android Studio or Vietnam Team 25242 writes their autonomous routine, they are doing it on machines that were headed for a Wisconsin storage closet eighteen months earlier. The same machines that sat idle in a Milliman office in 2023 are now running FTC dashboards in Arizona and powering after-school coding sessions at the Milwaukee Robotics Academy. The arithmetic is blunt: zero marginal hardware cost to the recipient, zero landfill waste, and a student who can actually write code on a real computer instead of sharing one between six people.
whyItMatters.callout: From 9 laptops in our first season to 56 this year — a program that was an experiment in 2022 is now a structured supply chain reaching four continents. The growth is not coincidental: every season we have refined the intake process, deepened partner relationships, and expanded the distribution network to match the real demand that exists in underserved FIRST programs worldwide.

pipeline.label: Collect
pipeline.summary: Community drives and partner donations bring machines in.
pipeline.detail: The pipeline begins before we touch a single screw. We run collection drives through partner organizations — libraries, corporate sponsors like Milliman and Reserve Advisors, and local businesses including Soerens Ford — to gather machines that would otherwise sit forgotten in storage closets or get sent to a landfill. We put the word out broadly, making it easy for individuals, offices, and schools to hand over old laptops without worrying about data — that part is our job. Each collection point is coordinated in advance so machines arrive in manageable batches rather than overwhelming our workflow. Over five seasons we have learned that the quality and consistency of incoming hardware directly determines what we can ship downstream, so we also turn away machines too old or broken to make the cut, keeping our refurbishing pipeline efficient and our recipients satisfied.
highlights: Coordinated drives with Milliman, Reserve Advisors, Soerens Ford, and local libraries
Machines collected from individuals, offices, and schools across the Brookfield area
Clear intake criteria — machines too old or damaged are responsibly redirected
Batched collection schedule to match our refurbishing capacity
No data concerns for donors — secure wipe happens in our pipeline

pipeline.label: Inventory
pipeline.summary: Every machine is logged, tested, and triaged before any work begins.
pipeline.detail: Before a laptop enters the refurbishing queue, it goes through a structured intake check. We log make, model, processor, RAM, storage, and any visible hardware issues. Each machine is powered on and assessed: does the battery hold a charge, does the keyboard respond, does the display show dead pixels, do the ports function? Machines that pass this triage move to the wipe queue. Those that fail are assessed further — a machine with a bad battery but working internals might have its drive reimaged and go to a fixed-power use case; a machine with a cracked motherboard is parted out or responsibly recycled. This step keeps the downstream process predictable: every machine that enters the wipe station has already been screened, so we are not discovering surprises mid-install. Good inventory hygiene has been one of the biggest operational lessons of the program — it is what allows us to scale without losing quality control.
highlights: Each machine logged: make, model, RAM, storage, processor generation
Full hardware triage — battery, display, keyboard, ports, boot test
Clear pass/fail/triage criteria for each hardware category
Failed machines parted out or recycled — none go to landfill
Inventory log feeds directly into the distribution matching step

pipeline.label: Wipe + New OS
pipeline.summary: A clean slate: every drive wiped, every machine re-imaged.
pipeline.detail: This is the technical core of the program. Every machine that passes triage gets a multi-pass secure erase — the previous owner's data is gone before we touch anything else. We then install a fresh operating system: for machines going to FTC teams, Blair Tech licenses give us Windows installs that are legitimate, activated, and ready to run Android Studio, FTC Dashboard, and the team's build toolchain out of the box. For machines going to general education programs — Milwaukee Robotics Academy, Tech Lit Africa partner sites, and others — we evaluate on a case-by-case basis: Windows where the license covers it, a hardened Linux distribution on older hardware that benefits from a lighter OS. Every install is then validated: the machine boots cleanly, connects to Wi-Fi, installs a test application, and gets a final hardware-functionality pass before it is cleared for distribution. We do not ship machines that we would not be comfortable handing to a student ourselves.
highlights: Multi-pass secure drive erase — zero previous-owner data remains
Blair Tech licenses for Windows installs on team-bound machines
Linux options evaluated for older hardware to maximize useful life
Full post-install validation: boot, Wi-Fi, test app, hardware pass
Machines are FTC-ready (Android Studio, FTC SDK, build tools) where applicable

pipeline.label: Distribute
pipeline.summary: Machines matched to recipients and shipped worldwide.
pipeline.detail: Distribution is where the work becomes real. Each refurbished machine is matched to a specific recipient based on what that program needs: FTC teams in underserved regions need machines that can run Android Studio; community education programs need reliable general-purpose laptops; library programs need machines that handle web browsing and document editing without issues. We coordinate with receiving contacts — coaches, program directors, Tech Lit Africa's in-country logistics — to ensure machines arrive at the right time in the right condition. International shipments require additional documentation and coordination, and we have built up the process knowledge over multiple seasons to handle it smoothly. The last step in the pipeline is also its most motivating: hearing from a team in Libya or Vietnam that the machines arrived and are running their FTC code is the direct feedback loop that keeps the program scaling each year.
highlights: Each machine matched to a specific recipient program based on technical requirements
FTC-ready machines prioritized for FTC teams in underserved regions
International shipping coordination with Tech Lit Africa and in-country contacts
Receiving confirmation collected from every recipient organization
Direct feedback loop — team hears from recipients when machines are in use
